africanelephant: An African bush elephant, large fan-shaped ears, a long grey trunk hanging down with the tip curled inward, two separate curved white tusks emerging from the sides of the mouth clearly below and apart from the trunk, trunk and tusks not touching, all four legs clearly separated, standing on savanna
asianelephant: An Asian elephant, smaller rounded ears, arched back, a long grey trunk with a single fingerlike tip hanging separately from short tusks, trunk and tusks not touching, all four legs clearly separated, standing on forest ground
mammoth: A woolly mammoth, thick shaggy reddish-brown fur, high domed head, two long curved tusks sweeping outward and separate from its trunk, trunk hanging freely not touching the tusks, all four legs clearly separated, standing on tundra
walrus: A walrus, massive wrinkled brown-pink body, two long white downward tusks, thick whiskers, lying on ice
sealion: A California sea lion, sleek brown body, external ear flaps, long front flippers propping its chest up, resting on a rock
fursealion: A South African fur seal, dense brown fur, pointed muzzle, external ear flaps, propped up on its front flippers
elephantseal: A southern elephant seal, massive grey-brown blubbery body, males with a large inflatable proboscis nose, lying on a beach
leopardseal: A leopard seal, a very long slender serpentine seal with a remarkably elongated sinuous neck and a massive REPTILIAN head, broad and blunt like a lizard's, carrying an enormous wide gaping jaw far larger than any other seal's. Silvery-grey above and pale below, spotted with dark blotches over the throat and shoulders, with long slender fore-flippers. Long snake-necked and huge-headed, not a small round-headed harbour seal
weddellseal: A Weddell seal resting on ice, an extremely plump rotund barrel-shaped seal whose head is strikingly SMALL for its huge body, with a short blunt cat-like face, large dark eyes, long pale whiskers, and a distinctly upcurved mouthline giving a permanent gentle smile. Mottled silver-grey blotched with darker and paler patches. Tiny head on a very fat body
harpseal: An adult harp seal on ice, a silvery pale grey seal whose face and head are solid BLACK like a mask, and whose back carries a bold black HARP-shaped saddle: a broad curved wishbone or horseshoe band sweeping back from each shoulder and meeting over the spine to form a single large dark harp marking. The black face and the harp-shaped back band are essential
ribbonseal: A ribbon seal, dark body with bold pale ribbon-shaped bands around the neck, shoulders, and hindquarters, resting on ice
monkseal: A Hawaiian monk seal, grey-brown sleek body, short flippers, resting on a sandy beach
crabeaterseal: A crabeater seal resting on ice, a slim elongated seal with a long slender body, a narrow pointed muzzle turned slightly UPWARD at the tip, and a pale silvery-blonde to creamy white coat marked with scattered darker mottling and old pale scars along its flanks. Slender and pale, not a plump uniformly grey seal
bluewhale: A blue whale seen from the side, an immensely long slender whale of mottled blue-grey, its body drawn out long and tapering, with a very broad flat U-shaped rostrum like a wide rounded shield seen from above, a single prominent ridge running from blowhole to snout tip, long pleated throat grooves, and a tiny stubby dorsal fin set very far back near the tail. Enormously elongated with a small far-back fin, not a stocky whale with a large dorsal
humpback: A humpback whale, long white pectoral fins, knobby tubercles on the head, dark grey body, breaching gently at the surface
finwhale: A fin whale, sleek grey-brown streamlined body, asymmetrical jaw coloring, small hooked dorsal fin, swimming near the surface
minke: A minke whale, small sleek dark grey body, pointed rostrum, white band on the pectoral fin, swimming near the surface
seiwhale: A sei whale, sleek dark steel-grey body, tall curved dorsal fin, streamlined shape, swimming near the surface
brydeswhale: A Bryde's whale seen from the side, a slender dark smoky-grey rorqual with a pale underside, long pleated throat grooves, a tall curved sickle-shaped dorsal fin set about two thirds back, and, uniquely, THREE parallel ridges running side by side along the top of the rostrum from the blowholes to the snout tip rather than a single central ridge. The three rostral ridges are its distinguishing feature
rightwhale: A right whale, stocky black body, distinctive rough white callosities on the head, no dorsal fin, swimming near the surface
bowhead: A bowhead whale, massive black body, strongly arched jawline, no dorsal fin, swimming near Arctic ice
graywhale: A gray whale seen from the side, a mottled slate-grey whale blotched with pale patches and encrusted with clusters of barnacles and whale lice around the head and back. Its back carries NO dorsal fin at all, only a low broad hump about two thirds of the way along, followed by a row of small bumpy knuckles running down the spine to the tail. A narrow bowed rostrum. The absence of a dorsal fin is essential
spermwhale: A sperm whale seen from the side, dominated by an ENORMOUS squared-off blocky rectangular head making up fully a third of its entire length, a huge blunt box that ends in a flat vertical wall at the front, beneath which runs a narrow underslung rod-like lower jaw much smaller than the head above it. Dark grey wrinkled prune-like skin along the flanks, small paddle flippers, and a low rounded hump followed by knuckles along the spine instead of a dorsal fin. The vast squared box head and narrow jaw are essential: it must not be a humpback or a smooth-headed whale with throat pleats and long flippers
orca: An orca, glossy black body with sharp white eye patches, white chin and belly, pale grey saddle patch behind the dorsal fin, tall black dorsal fin, swimming near the surface
pilotwhale: A long-finned pilot whale, dark black-grey bulbous rounded head, curved dorsal fin, swimming near the surface. Plain empty white background: no grey panel, no box, no square backdrop, no border, no ground, no scenery of any kind behind the animal.
falsekiller: A false killer whale, uniform dark grey-black slender body, rounded head, curved dorsal fin, swimming near the surface
melonhead: A melon-headed whale, dark grey slender body, rounded melon-shaped head with a pointed snout, tall dorsal fin, swimming near the surface
beluga: A beluga whale, all-white rounded body, bulbous forehead melon, no dorsal fin, swimming near the surface
narwhal: A narwhal seen from the side, a stocky mottled grey-and-white whale with a single long straight spiralled ivory tusk projecting forward from the left side of its head, a small rounded head with no beak, and short rounded flippers. Its back is completely smooth with NO dorsal fin at all, carrying only a low shallow ridge along the spine. The absence of a dorsal fin is essential
bottlenose: A bottlenose dolphin seen from the side, a sleek muscular grey dolphin with a short thick well-defined stubby beak clearly set off from a rounded bulging melon by a distinct crease, an upcurved mouthline giving a permanent smile, a tall curved sickle dorsal fin, and counter-shaded colouring from dark grey above through soft grey flanks to a pale cream belly
spinnerdolphin: A spinner dolphin, slender grey body with a long thin beak, tall triangular dorsal fin, swimming near the surface
duskydolphin: A dusky dolphin, dark grey back with pale grey and white flank markings, curved dorsal fin, swimming near the surface
hectorsdolphin: A Hector's dolphin, small stocky grey body, distinctive rounded black dorsal fin shaped like a mouse ear, swimming near the surface
commersons: A Commerson's dolphin, bold black and white patterned body, rounded dorsal fin, swimming near the surface
rissos: A Risso's dolphin seen from the side, a robust grey dolphin whose head is BLUNT and bulbous, rounded off at the front with no beak or snout whatsoever, and split by a distinct vertical crease running down the centre of the melon. Its pale grey body is criss-crossed all over with dense white scratches and scars, and it carries a tall curved dorsal fin. The beakless blunt head and heavy scarring are essential: it must not have a dolphin's protruding beak
irrawaddy: An Irrawaddy dolphin seen from the side, a pale bluish-grey dolphin with a rounded blunt bulging forehead and no beak at all, a visible neck crease behind the head, a rounded mouthline giving a faint smile, and a very SMALL low rounded dorsal fin set well back and barely rising from the back
amazonriverdolphin: An Amazon river dolphin, pale pink long-beaked body, small dorsal ridge, flexible neck, swimming in murky river water
gangesdolphin: A Ganges river dolphin, grey long narrow beaked body, tiny eyes, small triangular dorsal hump, swimming in river water
vaquita: A vaquita, small grey porpoise body, distinctive dark rings around the eyes and lips, small triangular dorsal fin, swimming near the surface
harborporpoise: A harbor porpoise, small stocky grey-brown body, blunt rounded snout, small triangular dorsal fin, swimming near the surface
cuvierbeaked: A Cuvier's beaked whale seen from the side, a robust cigar-shaped whale with a short stubby goose-like beak and a gently sloping forehead, its body rich brown fading to a distinctly PALE CREAM-WHITE head and back of the neck, and covered all over in white linear scratches and oval pale scars, with two small teeth showing at the tip of the lower jaw and a small dorsal fin set far back
manatee: A West Indian manatee, large grey wrinkled rounded body, paddle-shaped tail, whiskered snout, swimming slowly underwater
dugong: A dugong, smooth grey streamlined body, downturned bristled snout, fluked whale-like tail, swimming underwater
capybara: A capybara, large barrel-shaped brown body, blunt squared snout, no visible tail, standing at a riverbank
porcupine: A North American porcupine, stocky body covered in long sharp quills mixed with dark fur, standing on a log
chinchilla: A chinchilla sitting up, a small rodent with extraordinarily dense plush silver-grey fur that looks impossibly thick and soft, a rounded head with very large round ears, enormous black eyes, long fine whiskers, and a bushy squirrel-like tail. Its fur density and huge round ears are essential: it must not read as a plain rabbit
prairiedog: A black-tailed prairie dog sitting upright on its haunches in an alert sentry posture with its small forepaws held together at its chest, a plump rounded body covered in a uniform sandy tan-buff coat over its whole chest and belly with no dark patch, small rounded ears, dark eyes, and a short tail tipped with black. Its front must be plain pale tan: no dark grey slab, no black bib and no shadow across the chest
groundhog: A groundhog standing on all four legs, a heavy-bodied thickset marmot with a low chunky body close to the ground, short powerful legs with heavy digging claws, a broad blunt head with small rounded ears, grizzled brown fur with coarse frosted guard hairs, and a short bushy tail
redsquirrel: A red squirrel, reddish-orange fur, bushy tail, tufted ears, sitting upright on a tree branch
flyingsquirrel: A flying squirrel gliding horizontally through the air, a small squirrel with a loose furry skin membrane, the patagium, stretched taut between its outstretched front and hind legs on each side to form a soft square furry glider surface edged with fur, its body held flat and level, with enormous round black eyes and a broad flattened bushy tail trailing behind as a rudder. The membrane is a furry flap of skin joining wrist to ankle: it must NOT be a bat wing with visible finger bones or leathery struts, and the animal must not stand upright on two legs
chipmunk: An eastern chipmunk, reddish-brown fur with bold black and white stripes down the back, sitting upright with cheek pouches
dormouse: A hazel dormouse, golden-orange fur, large black eyes, long furry tail, sitting on a branch holding a hazelnut
jerboa: A long-eared jerboa, a tiny tan desert rodent with enormous ears, a long tufted tail and very long thin hind legs, crouched low on its hind feet with its small forepaws tucked against its chest, seen from the side. A small animal, not humanoid, no hands on hips, no upright human posture.
marmot: An alpine marmot, stocky brown-furred body, short legs, sitting upright on a rocky alpine meadow
viscacha: A mountain viscacha perched on rock, a rodent that looks like a rabbit crossed with a squirrel, with long upright rounded ears, a blunt rounded face with long whiskers and a dark stripe, dense soft grey-brown fur with a paler belly, and a very long bushy squirrel-like tail curling up behind it
agouti: An agouti standing on all four legs, a large rodent with an arched hunched back and hindquarters carried higher than the shoulders, standing on slender delicate hoof-like toes, with a blunt rounded muzzle, small rounded ears, glossy coarse grizzled orange-brown fur that is brightest and most coppery over the rump, and almost no visible tail
mara: A Patagonian mara standing on all four legs, a large long-legged rodent shaped like a cross between a hare and a small deer, with a blunt rounded rabbit-like muzzle, upright ears SHORTER and more rounded than a hare's, slender hoof-like feet, a grey-brown coat, and a distinctive white patch across the rump edged above by a dark band, with almost no visible tail
nakedmolerat: A naked mole-rat lying flat on all four legs along the floor of an earth tunnel, its body a small pink sausage lying horizontally, hairless with loose wrinkled saggy translucent skin folding along its tubular body, tiny almost invisible pinprick eyes, no ears, and short stubby legs splayed to the sides. Projecting FORWARD from the front of its mouth outside the lips are two pairs of large flat chisel-like buck teeth, an upper pair and a lower pair meeting like pincers, jutting forward like a digging tool and not downward like walrus tusks. It is a burrowing rodent on its belly: not standing upright, no human body, no human face, no arms, shoulders or chest
degu: A degu, a small stocky brown rodent with a compact body, large rounded ears, big dark eyes, and a long thin tail ending in a distinct BLACK tufted brush at the tip like a bottle brush, sitting up on its haunches
hare: A brown hare, tawny-brown fur, very long black-tipped ears, powerful long hind legs, sitting alert in a field
arctichare: An arctic hare sitting on snow, a heavily built compact hare with a thick rounded body and unusually SHORT ears for a hare, tipped with black at the very ends, and dense deep pure white winter fur that looks thick and plush all over. Chunky and short-eared, not a slim long-eared brown hare
pika: A pika perched on rock, a very small round ball-shaped animal with a compact rounded body, large rounded mouse-like ears set on the sides of the head, a blunt short muzzle, short legs and NO visible tail at all, with dense grizzled grey-brown fur
ninebandarmadillo: A nine-banded armadillo, grey-brown segmented bony armor plating, pointed snout, standing on forest floor
giantarmadillo: A giant armadillo, large brown-grey heavily armored segmented body, huge front claws, standing on dirt
giantanteater: A giant anteater, coarse grizzled grey fur with a bold black-and-white diagonal stripe, elongated snout, huge bushy tail, standing on grassland
tamandua: A tamandua, tan fur with a black vest-shaped patch over the shoulders and back, long snout, prehensile tail, climbing a tree
silkyanteater: A silky anteater, golden silky fur, tiny curled body, prehensile tail, gripping a thin branch
platypus: A platypus, streamlined brown furred body, flat rubbery duck-like bill, webbed feet, swimming at the surface of a stream
echidna: A short-beaked echidna, round body covered in cream spines mixed with fur, long thin snout, standing on forest ground
greatwhite: A great white shark, robust grey countershaded body with a white underside, triangular serrated teeth visible, tall dorsal fin, swimming
whaleshark: A whale shark seen from the side, whose SHAPE is unlike any ordinary shark: an enormously broad flat squared-off head far wider than its body, blunt and flattened like a wide plank with no pointed snout at all, carrying a huge straight mouth stretched right across the very FRONT edge of the head from corner to corner rather than tucked underneath, and tiny eyes set far out at the extreme corners of the head. Three prominent raised ridges run the length of each flank from behind the head to the tail. Its dark blue-grey back is covered in a bold regular CHECKERBOARD pattern: rows of evenly spaced pale cream-white round spots arranged in a neat grid between pale vertical and horizontal stripes, like a chessboard laid over its back, with a plain white belly. The flat wide plank-shaped head, the front-facing mouth, the flank ridges and the gridded checkerboard spots are all essential: it must not look like an ordinary pointed-snouted grey shark with scattered dots
hammerhead: A great hammerhead shark, distinctive wide flattened hammer-shaped head with eyes positioned at each end of the flattened extensions, grey countershaded body, tall dorsal fin, swimming
tigershark: A tiger shark, blue-grey body with dark vertical stripes fading toward the tail, blunt rounded snout, swimming
bullshark: A bull shark, stocky grey robust body, blunt rounded snout, small eyes, swimming near the surface
makoshark: A shortfin mako shark seen from the side, a sharply streamlined fast shark with a sharply pointed conical snout, large solid black eyes, and a stiff crescent-shaped tail. Its colouring is a brilliant metallic indigo-blue over the back and upper flanks ending in a crisp sharply defined line against a bright white underside. Vivid metallic blue above and white below, not a uniform dull grey
thresher: A thresher shark, slender grey body, extremely elongated scythe-like upper tail lobe nearly as long as its body, swimming
baskingshark: A basking shark seen from the side swimming with its mouth open, the mouth gaping into an ENORMOUS round cavernous circular opening far taller than the rest of its head and wide enough to swallow the whole front of the animal, lined with pale bristly gill rakers and no large sharp teeth. Gigantic gill slits run so far around the head that they nearly encircle it, almost meeting at the throat. A conical pointed snout above the mouth, tiny eyes, and a greyish-brown mottled body. The vast round filter-feeding mouth and the wrap-around gill slits are essential: it must not be a great white shark with a toothy jaw
nurseshark: A nurse shark resting on the sea floor, a broad-headed bottom-dwelling shark with a wide flattened blunt rounded head, small eyes, two fleshy whisker-like barbels hanging from its nostrils above the mouth, and large rounded soft-cornered fins. Its colour is a muted greyish-brown to dull tan-brown, natural and drab, not bright yellow and not golden
reefshark: A grey reef shark, sleek grey body, dark tips on the dorsal and tail fins, swimming near a coral reef
goblinshark: A goblin shark seen from the side, with distinctly PINK pale flabby soft-looking skin, a long flat blade-shaped snout projecting far forward over its mouth like a paddle or a spade, and highly protrusible jaws thrust right out and away from the head on a stalk of gum, lined with long thin needle-like fangs. A soft flabby body and small low fins. The pink colour, the long flat overhanging blade snout, and the jaws jutting out from the face are all essential
frilledshark: A frilled shark seen from the side, shaped like an EEL rather than a shark: an extremely long slender serpentine snake-like body of even thickness winding along its length, with all its small fins set far back near the tail and no large triangular dorsal fin. Its flattened head carries a wide mouth opening at the very FRONT tip of the snout rather than underneath, and six pairs of frilly ruffled gill slits with fringed edges wrapping around the throat like a collar. Dark chocolate-brown. It must look like an eel or a sea serpent, not like an ordinary torpedo-shaped shark
wobbegong: A tasselled wobbegong, flattened mottled brown-patterned body, ornate fringe of skin flaps around the jaw, resting camouflaged on the sea floor
greenlandshark: A Greenland shark seen from the side, a heavy sluggish deep-water shark with a thick stout cylindrical body, a short blunt rounded snout, very small eyes, and unusually small low rounded fins including a tiny dorsal fin, giving it a soft heavy shapeless look. Uniform dark slate grey-brown, slightly mottled. Stout blunt and slow-looking, not a streamlined sharp-finned predatory shark
zebrashark: A zebra shark, pale body covered in dark spots as an adult, long ridged tail, resting on the sea floor
epaulette: An epaulette shark, slender brown spotted body with a large dark eyespot behind each pectoral fin, walking on its fins over a reef
mantaray: A giant manta ray seen from above, an enormous flattened diamond with long tapering triangular wings far wider than the body is long, a wide straight mouth across the very front of the head, and two distinctive CEPHALIC FINS, a pair of fleshy horn-like paddles curling forward from either side of the mouth like horns. Black above with a white underside and a slender whip tail. Natural black and white colouring, not tinted cyan or turquoise
stingray: A southern stingray, flat diamond-shaped grey-brown body, long whip-like tail, gliding just above sandy sea floor
eagleray: A spotted eagle ray seen from above, a broad diamond-shaped ray with long pointed swept-back wings, a distinctive protruding flattened DUCK-BILL snout at the front of the head, and a very long thin whip-like tail several times the length of its body. Deep blue-black above covered in dense evenly spaced white rings and spots, with a white underside
sawfish: A smalltooth sawfish, flattened grey-brown body, long flat blade-like snout lined with paired teeth, swimming near the sea floor
electricray: An electric torpedo ray seen from above, shaped as a smooth completely ROUND disc, an even unbroken circle of soft fleshy body like a plate, with no points, no spikes and no projecting snout anywhere on its outline, its small eyes set on top near the front and a short thick fleshy tail behind carrying two small rounded fins. Plain muddy grey-brown above. Its outline must read as a clean smooth circle, not a pointed or angular shape and not a spike
clownfish: A clownfish, orange body with white bars edged in black, swimming among sea anemone tentacles
mandarinfish: A mandarinfish, small body covered in intricate wavy patterns of blue, orange, and green, swimming near coral rubble
lionfish: A red lionfish, striped red and white body, dramatic fan-like venomous spiny fins spread wide, swimming near a reef
pufferfish: A pufferfish, round spotted body, small fins, large eyes, swimming near a reef
boxfish: A yellow boxfish, rigid box-shaped yellow body covered in dark spots, small fins, swimming near a reef
parrotfish: A parrotfish, vivid blue-green scaled body, beak-like fused teeth, swimming near a coral reef
wrasse: A cleaner wrasse, slender blue body with a black horizontal stripe, swimming near a coral reef
triggerfish: A clown triggerfish seen from the side, a deep oval compressed fish with a distinctly lozenge-shaped body, its LOWER half boldly marked with large round white polka dots on black while the upper back carries a fine yellow crosshatched net pattern, a bright yellow-orange mouth, and a stout first dorsal spine standing up as a locking trigger on its back. The white spots belong on the lower half, not scattered evenly all over
angelfish: An emperor angelfish, bold blue and yellow horizontal stripes, dark mask across the eyes, swimming near a coral reef
butterflyfish: A copperband butterflyfish seen from the side, a very tall thin disc-shaped fish compressed flat like a plate, banded with vertical copper-orange and white stripes, with a long narrow tweezer-like snout, a dark bar running down through the real eye to hide it, and a distinct round black false EYESPOT near the base of the tail at the rear of the dorsal fin
